title: Dhamaal 4 Just Opened to ₹12 Crore. But the Real Show Was the Ghost Who Came Back.
excerpt: Satish Kaushik’s digital resurrection as Bata Bhai opens the franchise’s biggest box office day in seven years — and the diaspora is eating it up from Sydney to New Jersey.
body:
The lights went down. The audience went quiet. And then Satish Kaushik walked back onto the screen.

<youtube></youtube>

Not a body double. Not archival footage. A full, digital resurrection of the actor who died suddenly in March 2023, reprising his iconic **Bata Bhai** from *Double Dhamaal* — brought back through a blend of high-end CGI and artificial intelligence, with permission and support from his wife, **Shashi Kaushik**, who is thanked personally in the opening credits. If you grew up quoting Bata Bhai’s underworld one-liners over dinner tables from Dallas to Dubai, you were not prepared for this.

And then **Dhamaal 4** got loud.

## The Franchise Hits Double Digits

The fourth installment in India’s most lovably absurd comedy franchise opened across theatres on July 10 to the kind of numbers that make the trade sit up: **₹11.88 crore net** across 10,668 tracked shows, bringing the India gross to **₹14.02 crore** by the final night shows. Nearly **two lakh tickets** sold on BookMyShow alone, with evening shows hitting a 24.85% occupancy rate — nearly triple the morning numbers.

For context, the entire Dhamaal franchise has now collectively grossed approximately ₹355 crore across its three prior installments. *Total Dhamaal* opened at ₹16.50 crore on a regular Friday in 2019. The fourth part is tracking right alongside that benchmark, with strong walk-in business suggesting the final Day 1 tally could push even higher once late-night data is compiled.

Overseas, the film is already leading in key diaspora markets. In **Australia**, it opened at 84K AUD, comfortably ahead of *Welcome to the Jungle* (51K AUD) and *Cocktail 2* (77.6K AUD). In **New Zealand**, it nearly doubled the competition with 46K NZD. For an Indian comedy franchise without a single A-list actress or romantic subplot, those numbers in the diaspora are telling — this audience doesn’t want polished. They want their boys back.

## Sea Pirates, Supernatural Madness, and a Treasure Worth ₹50 Crore

The formula has changed. Gone is the multi-story race-to-the-money structure of *Total Dhamaal*. This time, director **Indra Kumar** throws the gang into a full-blown maritime treasure hunt involving sea pirates and supernatural elements, as **Ajay Devgn’s** sharp-witted Guddu Rastogi, **Arshad Warsi’s** Aditya, **Jaaved Jaaferi’s** endearingly dim Manav, and **Riteish Deshmukh’s** eccentric Deshbandhu chase a ₹50 crore haul.

Joining the chaos: **Ravi Kishan** as the antagonist pirate captain Michael, **Sanjay Mishra** as Johnny D’Costa, and a fresh contingent of **Sanjeeda Shaikh**, **Esha Gupta**, and **Anjali Anand** — the last of whom is already drawing praise for her turn as Paaro.

> “Dhamaal 4 lives up to its title, taking the madness to an altogether new level. LOL moments in the first half, excellent post-interval, with tadka of emotions in climax. Don’t look for logic — this one’s a stressbuster.” — **Taran Adarsh**, ⭐⭐⭐½


The CBFC gave it a UA 13+ rating with zero cuts — rare for a Bollywood comedy these days. Trade analyst **Joginder Tuteja** specifically noted that the humor is designed for kids, calling that “so rare in Bollywood today” and flagging a HIT if the second half holds up. By evening, the consensus was clear: it held up.

## Why the Diaspora Keeps Coming Back to Dhamaal

There is something about this franchise that transcends the usual Bollywood comedy formula. The original *Dhamaal* (2007) was a shamelessly silly riff on *It’s a Mad, Mad, Mad, Mad World*, and it became a cult favourite precisely because it refused to be anything else. No romantic angle. No message. Just four idiot friends, a treasure, and escalating chaos. It’s the kind of film that plays on loop at every NRI house party, the kind of film your cousin in New Jersey quotes entirely in Arshad Warsi’s voice.

The fact that the franchise still commands double-digit openings nearly two decades later — without relying on a holiday window, a star heroine, or global pre-release buzz — says something about what Indian audiences abroad are actually hungry for: familiarity, warmth, and the particular brand of chaos that only Indian comedy delivers at its best.

The digital Satish Kaushik tribute is the emotional core of that appeal. It’s not just an opening sequence. It’s a reminder that this franchise knows its audience is watching with 20 years of affection. Indra Kumar has turned that affection into box office gold.

## What’s Next

The weekend numbers will be decisive. If *Dhamaal 4* holds steady through Saturday and Sunday — particularly with family crowds expected to surge — a ₹50 crore opening weekend is firmly within reach. The real question is whether it has the legs to challenge *Total Dhamaal’s* lifetime of ₹154 crore, or whether the packed summer window (with *Cocktail 2*, *Alpha*, and *Welcome to the Jungle* all fighting for the same screens) clips its run short.

For now, the boys are back. And so is Bata Bhai.
